item.title: More people are getting the flu. Should you get a flu shot before you travel?
item.description: Thanksgiving is just around the corner, just as millions of Americans are expected to travel for the holidays. Another thing that's upon us? Cold and flu season.

item.title: Health organization to announce that the U.S. has lost its measles elimination status
item.description: The Pan American Health Organization is expected to announce that measles is no longer eliminated in the U.S. Record cases, lower vaccination rates and uncontained outbreaks led to the resurgence.
item.content:encoded: The Pan American Health Organization is expected to announce that measles is no longer eliminated in the U.S. Record cases, lower vaccination rates and uncontained outbreaks led to the resurgence.

item.title: Why sleep matters when it comes to weight gain and loss
item.description: Sleep can have a powerful impact on weight. Research shows it can affect appetite. There is also a two-way relationship between sleep quality and diet.

item.title: What's the real cost of fast fashion? Ask the people making your jeans
item.description: Sydney Sweeney has great jeans, American Eagle Outfitters tells us. But who made them? And what are working conditions like in the garment factories of Pakistan and Bangladesh?

item.title: Laws limiting coal miners' exposure to toxic dust are in danger of being rolled back
item.description: Coal miners who are exposed to silica dust are at a higher risk of black lung disease. Despite decades of advocacy, new efforts to regulate the toxic dust are under threat.

item.title: US has lost measles elimination status, global health authorities say
item.description: The U.S. has lost its status as a country where measles is eliminated, according to researchers with direct knowledge of the deliberations at the Pan American Health Organization.

item.title: A new policy could help solve the U.S. organ shortage. Critics say it's unethical
item.description: New guidelines are supposed to protect organ donors in a retrieval procedure that keeps blood flowing through livers, kidneys, lungs and hearts. But bioethicists have troubling questions.
